sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is MBLUZ–P–5050, which includes a nearly complete skull and lower jaws.
This crocodilian possessed a long, narrow snout that comprised about 60% of the total skull length.
Its upper jaw bones held at least 20 teeth each, while the lower jaw bones held at least 23.
Siquisiquesuchus is an extinct genus of gavialid crocodilian named after the town of Siquisique in Lara, Venezuela, where the first specimens were found.
The genus was described by Christopher Brochu and Ascanio Rincón in 2004.
Researchers interpreted the presence of Siquisiquesuchus in South America as evidence that gavialoids dispersed across marine barriers to the Neotropics during the Tertiary period.
The genus Siquisiquesuchus is classified within the subfamily Gryposuchinae.
There is a debate regarding the classification of Siquisiquesuchus; some researchers classify it as a gryposuchinae gavialid, while others have not assigned it to a specific family or subfamily.
Siquisiquesuchus lived between 20.45 and 15.98 million years ago during the Burdigalian stage of the Miocene.
Fossils were found in Miocene-age rocks of the Castillo Formation in northwestern Venezuela.
The fossils were found in marginal marine deposits, suggesting a coastal habitat.
